name: Yellowy Green
lede: Yellowy Green is a plain compound name recorded by the 2010 xkcd color-name survey, not a historical dictionary entry.

sections.title: A phrase, not an entry
sections.body:
Paterson's dictionary uses the phrase "yellowy green" more than a dozen times, describing chrome green, Hooker's green, French green, jade green, sap green and spring green, among others, but it never lists Yellowy Green itself as a named color [1]. This hex, #BFF128, comes instead from the 2010 xkcd color-name survey, where thousands of people typed free-text names for colors shown on screen [2].

Its nearest look-alikes are [[lime]], 3.2 units away and more vivid, and [[lime-yellow]], 3.3 units away [3]. [[yellowish-green]], 4.4 units off, is darker [3]. The xkcd survey ran as a public web experiment rather than a curated dictionary, which is why its names, including this one, read as plain description rather than craft terminology [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: No painting in our 23,781-painting archive holds enough of this exact bright green to count as present, as photographed [4]. That reflects the limits of our archive's palette of older paintings, not a claim about the color itself [4].

origin.named_after: the modifier "yellowy" plus the color word green
